approval: Joe approved documented compatibility differences that keep user terminal commands inert, use validated cursor metadata, and handle tiny windows safely. This authorizes these safety expectations; it does not qualify the actual default boundary or close unrelated parity criteria.

approvedSafetyExpectations.rule: Every user ESC/C0/C1/DEL scalar in a source row is displayed as literal lowercase ASCII \uXXXX. User SGR/CSI/OSC/APC/DCS packets and Pi marker copies retain only data provenance. LF remains the authoritative source row boundary. Recalled HT is three spaces; source set/insert HT normalization remains four spaces.
approvedSafetyExpectations.explicitSourceDifference: Unsafe upstream packet execution, invisible controls, and forged first-marker cursor selection are deliberately not reproduced. The source map remains unchanged; escaped row positions are derived from its scalar source offsets. Safe expansion does not introduce another wrapping algorithm.

approvedSafetyExpectations.rule: Only a construction-sealed SourcePolicyId map authorizes the internally owned inverse span and anchor. Source segmentation selects the caret suffix. No APC marker is emitted; user text cannot authorize a style or hardware target. Hardware cursor is hidden; focused representable anchor is positioned for IME. Unfocused inverse appearance remains, without a hardware anchor.
approvedSafetyExpectations.explicitSourceDifference: A spoofed source marker cannot move the typed anchor. Native VT full/diff framing differs from TuiAltScreen; retained exact source component observations are a separate boundary.

approvedSafetyExpectations.rule: Source focus-preserving component crop handles heights1/2/3. Each row is bounded at whole grapheme edges without mutating the source draft or wrapping it again. Row/control expansion or component crop reports IsClipped. A caret whose full inverse selection does not fit is hidden and unanchored; resizing rebuilds it from the same unchanged draft.
approvedSafetyExpectations.explicitSourceDifference: Unplaceable carets and escaped control overflow do not emit invalid positions or unsafe packets. An indivisible CJK wider than the existing source map remains a pure builder ResourceLimit rather than upstream recursive failure; actual host recovery for this pre-factory failure remains lead-owned. Viewports outside declared existing limits fail before output.

approvedSafetyExpectations.rule: Transcript rows remain untrusted. Non-ASCII and controls are represented by literal ASCII \uXXXX/\UXXXXXXXX; backslashes are doubled. The newest bounded rows are bottom-aligned above the editor, and surplus row text is explicitly clipped. Transcript data cannot affect caret authority.
